title: The project's provider and model selection is committed configuration, with no local-only mode
statement: The selected provider, exact model identifier and thinking level are written to the project's `.pi/settings.json` and committed. There is no local-only override mode in which the selection is kept out of version control. What is never committed is anything host-specific or secret: credentials, the operator's consent to use this machine's connections, session transcripts, and compatibility records.
rationale: The selection is the answer to which model produced this project's content, and that answer belongs with the content. A local-only mode was floated in an earlier draft of the proposal and specified nowhere — no flag, no storage location, no precedence rule — which is the shape of a feature that sounds accommodating and has never been designed. Removing it also keeps one rule instead of two about what a clone inherits: configuration yes, consent no.

alternatives.option: Allow an operator to keep the provider and model out of the committed settings file
alternatives.whyNot: It would make the recorded content unattributable to a model and would need a second, uncommitted configuration location with its own precedence rules. The privacy concern it answers is met by the existing separation: the selection is not a secret, and the credential it authenticates against never appears in the file.

alternatives.option: Commit nothing and re-select on every machine
alternatives.whyNot: Turns a one-time decision into a prompt at every clone, and guarantees two operators on one project silently plan against different models.

notes: ⚠️ A COMMITTED SELECTION IS NOT A COMMITTED AUTHORISATION. Another operator inherits the choice of model and does not inherit permission to use this machine's credentials for it; that consent record lives in the ignored local-state root and its absence reopens the prompt.
